plain_description.what: Using the anchor-free tree (69 splits), this test asks which splits carry a gain in predicting which models answer correctly. A split is kept only if its gain beats its own chance level on training data and is still positive on held-out data.
plain_description.why: It asks whether model capability, not just text similarity, could be used to prune the tree, or whether only the top few splits matter.
plain_description.information: If only the trunk survived, the idea of building the tree around capability could be dropped. If more survive, the idea stays alive as a pruning step. Result: done. 20 of 69 splits survived, more than the 4 to 6 predicted, so the capability idea stays open, but only as a pruning step, never as a gate. Only 7 splits have a held-out gain clearly above zero. The splits kept this way overlap only weakly with the geometric certificate: the two select splits nearly independently of each other. Nothing was rebuilt or judged.
